newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac decorates rock star Johnny Hallyday.
newsitem.headline: Chirac decorates rock star Johnny Hallyday.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac pinned the red ribbon of the Legion of Honour on Friday on the lapel of rock star Johnny Hallyday, idolised in France for over 30 years as a Gallic answer to Elvis Presley.
Despite his stage name, Hallyday (real name Jean-Philippe Smet) is French and unknown in the United States where the newspaper USA Today once called him "the biggest rock star you've never heard."
Chirac said when decorating Hallyday, 53, for his contribution to the entertainement industry that he had become a real star by "merging the French and American cultures."
The president said he he had attended four of Hallyday's giant concerts. "I'm a real Johnny Hallyday fan," he said.

Hallyday, who spends an increasing part of the year in Florida, caused consternation among his fans earlier this month when a newspaper reported he was planning to seek American citizenship. He denied the report.
Hallyday has had huge success in a roller-coaster career as a rock star since a first hit in the early 1960s when General Charles de Gaulle was president of France.

Universally known as "Johnny", he was also a child television star in the mid-1950s. Hallyday made his American debut last year with a concert in Las Vegas -- but almost all the fans flew from France.
